causes.fix: Let the soil dry out fully before watering again. Check the pot has drainage holes and isn't sitting in a saucer of water.
Feed with a balanced or nitrogen-rich fertilizer, especially if older/lower leaves are yellowing first.
If it's just one or two older leaves, this can be normal. No action needed.

symptom_label: Wilting even though soil is moist

causes.fix: Remove plant from pot, check roots - brown/mushy roots mean root rot. Trim dead roots and repot in fresh, well-draining soil.
Move to a spot with afternoon shade during peak summer heat, even if the plant normally likes full sun.
If recently repotted or moved, give it a week to recover before changing anything else.

symptom_label: Brown, crispy leaf edges or tips

causes.fix: Increase watering frequency slightly and consider misting or grouping plants together to raise humidity.
Flush the soil with plain water and reduce fertilizer frequency - 'fertilizer burn' looks exactly like this.
Move away from harsh afternoon sun, especially for houseplants not adapted to full outdoor sun.

symptom_label: Plant looks leggy / stretched out with big gaps between leaves

causes.fix: Move to a brighter spot - closer to a window or into direct sun if the species tolerates it.
Pinch or trim the tips to encourage bushier, fuller growth.

symptom_label: Healthy looking plant but no flowers/fruit

causes.cause: Too much nitrogen, not enough phosphorus/potassium
causes.fix: Switch to a bloom-boosting fertilizer (higher middle/last number, e.g. 10-30-20).
Most flowering/fruiting plants need 6+ hours of direct sun - check actual sun exposure, not just 'bright' light.
Check the plant's typical days-to-maturity and planting season - it may simply not be time yet.

symptom_label: Small insects, webbing, or sticky residue on leaves

causes.fix: Spray with a mix of water + a few drops of dish soap, or wipe leaves with a cloth dipped in diluted neem oil. Repeat every few days.
Increase humidity and wipe leaves down; mites thrive in dry conditions. Neem oil spray helps here too.
Improve airflow around the plant, avoid wetting leaves when watering, and remove badly affected leaves. A diluted baking-soda spray can help mild cases.
Inspect leaves (including undersides) at dusk/dawn and hand-pick visible pests. Neem oil spray as a deterrent.
Check soil surface at night. Copper tape around pots or a shallow dish of beer nearby can help trap them.

causes.cause: Wrong season / soil too cold or too hot
causes.fix: Check the plant's ideal sowing months - many vegetables simply won't germinate outside their temperature range.
Keep soil consistently damp (not soaked) until germination - a covered tray or plastic wrap helps retain moisture.
Try a fresh seed packet from a different batch.
